attrs.name: extra
attrs.doc:
List of extra gnuplot commands. The commands will be inserted right before
     the plot command. Note that if you have multiple plots in the same command
     file, The extra commands may affect the subsequence plots.

attrs.name: where
attrs.doc:
File to store results in. By default, show them on a window. The format is
     determined from the file name extension: *.tex: LaTeX code with PostScript
     specials. *.eps: Encapsulated PostScript. *.pdf: Adobe PDF files. *.emf:
     Enhanced Metafile.
     The special name ’screen’ indicate that the data should be shown on the screen
     instead of being stored in a file.

attrs.name: title
attrs.doc: Title of the plot, if any. Set it to an empty string to disable.

attrs.name: device
attrs.doc: Output device. By default, this is derived from the file extenstion.

attrs.name: canvas
attrs.doc: Canvas size. By default, this depend on the device.

attrs.name: size
attrs.doc:
Relative to size of plot. The standard size is 1.0, specify other numbers to
        scale accordingly.
          <    x y    >
          – x : number (dimensionless)
            Parameter
            Relative horizontal size of plot.
          – y: number (dimensionless)
            Parameter
            Relative vertical size of plot.

attrs.name: legend
attrs.doc:
Placement of legend. This can be one of the four corners, named by compas
        locations (nw, ne, sw, se) to get the legend inside the graph in that corner,
        ’below’ to get the legend below the graph, ’outside’ to get the legend to the
        right of the graph, or ’none’ to avoid getting a legend at all.
        The value ’auto’ mean the legend will be places in the corner located farthest
        away from any data points. Note that datapoints outside the graph are ig-
        nored, and so are the lines connecting the datapoints. Thus, a line conncting
        two datapoints, one of them outside the graph, may cross the legend.

sections.name: soil
sections.desc:
A ‘common’ model (see 44.1, page 215) build into Daisy.
   Generate a 2D gnuplot graph with soil content.
sections.sig:
< soil     (file file )
             (top 0 [cm])
             (max max )
             (min min )
             (dimension dimension )
             (bottom bottom )
             (type block)
             (left 0 [cm])
             (right right )
             (missing missing ...)     ; Has default value.
             (filter)
             (original original ...)
             (dim line dim line )
             (when when )              ; Has partial value.
             (sizeratio -1 [])
             (use log false)
             (samples 25)
             ;; Shared parameters are described in section 44.1.
             (extra)
             (where screen)
             (title title )
             (device device )
             (canvas canvas )
             (size size )
             (legend auto) >

attrs.name: file
attrs.doc: Name of Daisy file where data is found.

attrs.name: top
attrs.doc: Higest z value in plot.

attrs.name: max
attrs.doc: Fixed highest value. By default determine this from the data.

attrs.name: min
attrs.doc: Fixed lowest value. By default determine this from the data.

attrs.name: dimension
attrs.doc: Dimension for data. By default, use dimension from file.

attrs.name: bottom
attrs.doc: Deepest z value in plot. By default, derive value from data file.

attrs.name: type
attrs.doc: Plot type. Valid options are ’block’ and ’contour’.

attrs.name: left
attrs.doc: Minimum x value in plot.

attrs.name: right
attrs.doc: Maximum x value in plot. By default, derive value from data file.

attrs.name: missing
attrs.doc:
(missing "" "00.00")
        Parameter description:
        List of strings indicating missing values.

attrs.name: filter
attrs.doc:
Only include data from rows that passes all these filters.
           <   tag allowed ...      >
           – tag: string (see section 4.1.5)
             Parameter
             Name of column in Daisy log file to filter for.
           – allowed : string (see section 4.1.5) sequence
             Parameter
             List of allowable values in filter.

attrs.name: original
attrs.doc:
List of dimensions of the data in the data file.
        If the list has only one element, that element is used as the dimension for
        all columns in the file. Otherwise, the list must have one element for each
        column.
        By default Daisy will use the names specified in data file.

attrs.name: dim line
attrs.doc:
If true, assume the line after the tags contain dimensions. By default this will
        be true iff ’original’ is not specified.

attrs.name: when
attrs.doc: Use value closest to this time.

attrs.name: sizeratio
attrs.doc:
If positive, ratio of y-axes length to x-axis length. If negative, use same ratio
        for units on the two axes.

attrs.name: use log
attrs.doc: log10 of each value

attrs.name: samples
attrs.doc: Number of sample lines for the ’smooth’ and ’contour’ types.

sections.text:
A ‘common’ model (see 44.1, page 215) build into Daisy.
   Generate a 2D gnuplot graph with soil content.

  < soil     (file file )
             (top 0 [cm])
             (max max )
             (min min )
             (dimension dimension )
             (bottom bottom )
             (type block)
             (left 0 [cm])
             (right right )
             (missing missing ...)     ; Has default value.
             (filter)
             (original original ...)
             (dim line dim line )
             (when when )              ; Has partial value.
             (sizeratio -1 [])
             (use log false)
             (samples 25)
             ;; Shared parameters are described in section 44.1.
             (extra)
             (where screen)
             (title title )
             (device device )
             (canvas canvas )
             (size size )
             (legend auto) >
   file: string (see section 4.1.5)
    Parameter
    Name of Daisy file where data is found.
   top: number [cm]
    Parameter (default 0)
    Higest z value in plot.
   max : number [<user>]
    Optional parameter
    Fixed highest value. By default determine this from the data.
   min: number [<user>]
    Optional parameter
    Fixed lowest value. By default determine this from the data.
   dimension: string (see section 4.1.5)
    Optional parameter
    Dimension for data. By default, use dimension from file.
   bottom: number [cm]
    Optional parameter
    Deepest z value in plot. By default, derive value from data file.
   type: string (see section 4.1.5)
    State variable (default ‘block’)
    Plot type. Valid options are ’block’ and ’contour’.
   left: number [cm]
    Parameter (default 0)
    Minimum x value in plot.

       right: number [cm]
        Optional parameter
        Maximum x value in plot. By default, derive value from data file.

       missing: string (see section 4.1.5) sequence
        Parameter (has default value with length 2)

        (missing "" "00.00")

        Parameter description:
        List of strings indicating missing values.

       filter : submodel (see section 4.1.7) sequence
        Submodel (default: an empty sequence)
        Only include data from rows that passes all these filters.
           <   tag allowed ...      >

           – tag: string (see section 4.1.5)
             Parameter
             Name of column in Daisy log file to filter for.
           – allowed : string (see section 4.1.5) sequence
             Parameter
             List of allowable values in filter.

       original : string (see section 4.1.5) sequence
        Optional parameter
        List of dimensions of the data in the data file.
        If the list has only one element, that element is used as the dimension for
        all columns in the file. Otherwise, the list must have one element for each
        column.
        By default Daisy will use the names specified in data file.

       dim line: boolean (see section 4.1.2)
        Optional parameter
        If true, assume the line after the tags contain dimensions. By default this will
        be true iff ’original’ is not specified.

       when: Time fixed component (see section 107.27)
        Submodel (has partially specified default value)
        Use value closest to this time.

       sizeratio: number (dimensionless)
        Parameter (default -1)
        If positive, ratio of y-axes length to x-axis length. If negative, use same ratio
        for units on the two axes.

       use log: boolean (see section 4.1.2)
        Parameter (default false)
        log10 of each value

       samples: integer
        Parameter (default 25)
        Number of sample lines for the ’smooth’ and ’contour’ types.
